open_points.subject: white-space policy value
open_points.text: The set is one value of the release; its home in the code, the data provider's constant the reading code imports (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1), is State 6's to give.
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name the imported constant that carries this decided white-space set instead of leaving its symbol to State 6.

open_points.subject: test release for disclosure-class enforcement
open_points.text: The check is made on every answer all the same, and it is shown on a test release whose class tables — the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant and the imported `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1) — differ from the first release's in the one row a test gives (Required tests 5 and 6).
open_points.question: How is the alternate release with changed imported class constants constructed for Required tests 5 and 6?
options: Generate a test-only data-provider module containing the alternate constants
Assemble a separate release artifact with the alternate constants
Parameterize generation and build each test release from a fixture
consequences: A test-only provider is small but requires the Factory to prove normal code imports it only in that test release.
A separate release most closely exercises release behavior but costs more assembly work.
Parameterized generation is reusable but introduces a Factory fixture interface.
open_points.requirement: On a test release whose class tables give a service a highest class below a class one of its answers carries, that answer is refused whole: no field of it is disclosed (rule 4).
open_points.default_guess: Generate an isolated test-release data provider and run the ordinary generated code against it.

open_points.subject: owner-interface host-name isolation
open_points.text: providing it and keeping every other HTTPS service of the host off it is a deployment step, carried to the deployment's owner (the Factory's platform deployment).
open_points.question: Which dedicated host name, DNS or hosts-file mapping, TLS endpoint and routing arrangement provide the owner interface's isolated host name?
options: A dedicated private DNS name terminated directly by Registry
A dedicated private DNS name terminated by a reverse proxy that routes only to Registry
A host-local name distributed through the owner's VPN configuration
consequences: Direct termination minimizes routing components but makes Registry responsible for the certificate endpoint.
A reverse proxy centralizes TLS but must guarantee that no other HTTPS service answers for the name.
A VPN-distributed local name avoids public DNS but couples access to VPN name distribution.
open_points.requirement: the deployment gives the owner interface a host name of its own, under which no other HTTPS service answers
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated private DNS name over the owner's VPN, with one TLS virtual host routed only to Registry.

open_points.subject: collision-after-step verification
open_points.text: the id Registry mints at random being the only way, which a test can arrange only by replacing the random source
open_points.question: How does the Factory replace or control the random source to create the post-step identifier collision without fixing a hidden production implementation seam in State 2?
options: Replace the random provider module during the check
Inject a deterministic random-value port in the generated assembly
Use a Factory-only instrumented build that returns a prescribed UUID
consequences: Module replacement keeps production contracts smaller but couples the check to module wiring.
Dependency injection exposes a stable seam but affects generated contracts and assembly.
An instrumented build isolates the seam but requires the Factory to prove it otherwise matches production generation.
open_points.requirement: A confirmation whose mapping, built in the confirming transaction, is not clean is refused whole and nothing changes
open_points.default_guess: Replace the generated random provider in a Factory-only check while exercising the normal confirmation path.

open_points.subject: code-level proof of clean-only import application
open_points.text: `confirm_import` builds the mapping inside the confirming transaction and applies it only when clean
open_points.question: Must generation expose a symbol literally named `confirm_import`, or may the Factory verify the required transactional behavior independently of generated function names?
options: Generate a function named `confirm_import` and let the Factory inspect it
Allow any generated symbol and verify behavior through declared wiring or instrumentation
Use a structural Factory rule over the transaction and mapping operations
consequences: A fixed name makes the check simple but turns a hidden implementation name into an accidental contract.
Behavioral verification preserves naming freedom but needs an observable transaction seam.
A structural rule avoids runtime fault injection but couples the Factory to generated-code structure.
open_points.requirement: A confirmation whose mapping, built in the confirming transaction, is not clean is refused whole and nothing changes
open_points.default_guess: Do not make the function name normative; verify the behavior through declared wiring and Factory instrumentation.

open_points.subject: snapshot-instant clock binding
open_points.text: The tests' clocks do not move between two reads of one run, so an implementation taking a backup's instant later than the read that fixes its snapshot (rule 1) is not told apart; that remains carried to Factory verification.
open_points.question: How does the Factory prove that the recorded backup instant is read at the same first store read that fixes the snapshot?
options: Use an instrumented clock that advances after every read and assert the recorded value
Trace the generated operation order around the first store read
Inject a store hook that advances the clock immediately after the snapshot-fixing read
consequences: An advancing clock gives a direct behavioral distinction but needs deterministic clock injection.
Structural tracing proves ordering but is coupled to generated-code shape.
A store hook closely targets the boundary but requires coordinated store and clock test seams.
open_points.requirement: the copy's read transaction fixes its snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected clock and a store hook that advances it immediately after the snapshot-fixing read.

set_aside.subject: owner-session monotonic instants
set_aside.text: held as readings of that monotonic clock
set_aside.question: What representation, precision and rounding rule do monotonic readings use when session, confirmation and lockout boundaries are compared?
options: Integer microseconds, rounded down
Integer nanoseconds
An exact duration type with a specified resolution
set_aside.default_guess: Integer microseconds, rounded down, matching the finest boundary the Required tests name.

witness.initial: An owner session has last_request at monotonic time 0 and expires at 30 minutes.
events: The owner sends a request at actual monotonic time 1799.9999996 seconds.
Registry represents the reading and compares it with the 1800-second boundary.
outcomes: A microsecond representation rounded down reads 1799.999999 and serves the request.
A microsecond representation rounded to nearest reads 1800.000000 and refuses the request.
witness.observer: The owner sees either the requested page or a sign-in refusal.

set_aside.subject: an admitted owner request
set_aside.text: Validity is checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1) — an upload, whose form sends its CSRF value before its file (A19 rule 4), arrives when that head, at most the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` constant, has been read (owner, 2026-11-17); a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs
set_aside.question: Does one monotonic reading both decide validity and become the request's new last-request instant, or may the operation read the clock again when updating that instant?
options: Take one reading at arrival and use it for both decisions
Take one reading for admission and a later reading for the last-request update
set_aside.default_guess: Take exactly one monotonic reading at arrival and use it for both admission and the new last-request instant.

witness.initial: A session's last_request is monotonic time 0 and its idle limit is 30 minutes.
events: A request begins its session check at 1799.999999 seconds and the check passes.
The clock reaches 1800.000001 seconds before the admitted request updates last_request.
The owner sends another request at 3599.999999 seconds.
outcomes: With one reading, last_request became 1799.999999 and the later request is exactly at its deadline, so it is refused.
With a second reading, last_request became 1800.000001 and the later request is still within its idle period, so it is served.
witness.observer: The owner sees either the requested page or a sign-in refusal.

set_aside.subject: failure to remove a newly created store
set_aside.text: A removal that fails, leaving an empty store of the release's version, cannot be made to happen through the surfaces without failing the store's making too; it is carried to Factory verification.
set_aside.question: How does the Factory cause only the cleanup removal to fail after successful store creation and listener failure?
options: Inject a filesystem adapter whose removal operation fails at the selected call
Instrument the generated filesystem call in a Factory-only build
Use operating-system permissions changed between creation and cleanup
consequences: An injected adapter is deterministic but requires a generation seam.
Instrumentation avoids a public seam but is coupled to generated calls.
Permission manipulation is closer to deployment behavior but can be platform-dependent and flaky.
set_aside.requirement: a start whose listener cannot be opened => it serves nothing, leaves no listener of it open, and the store holds the records it held before that start — for a store that start made new, no store, or, when its removal fails, an empty one holding no record but its audit sequence at 0   -- A17-4
set_aside.default_guess: Use a deterministic Factory-only filesystem adapter that fails the cleanup removal call.
